matters.text:
..Title
A Resolution amending Section 3.104(1) of Appendix A, Rules and Procedures of the Lexington-Fayette Urban County Council, pertaining to the order of business for Urban County Council Work Sessions, to change the label "Mayor's Report" to "Communications From the Mayor", to move the Communications From the Mayor to follow New Business Items on the order of business, and to add Donations, and Fixed Price Bids and Sole Source Procurements that only require the Urban County Government to enter into a unilateral Contract or issue a purchase order, as separate items for consideration under Communications From the Mayor, and relabeling or renumbering other affected items, all effective upon passage of Council. [Council Office, Hall] 

..Body 
      WHEREAS, the Urban County Council, by Resolution No. 55-79, as amended,  adopted "Rules and Procedures of the Lexington-Fayette Urban County Council", which were repealed, reorganized, revised and readopted by Resolution No. 599-2023 (hereinafter, "Rules"); 
      WHEREAS, Section 5.104 of the Rules provides that "[n]o permanent change shall be made to these rules without notice specifying the purpose and wording of the change given prior to the consideration of the change and the adoption of the permanent change by a majority of all councilmembers through an amending resolution"; and 
       WHEREAS, notice of proposed changes to the Rules was given to all Council members at the Council Work Session on May 7, 2024.
       NOW, THEREFORE, BE IT RESOLVED BY THE COUNCIL OF THE LEXINGTON-FAYETTE COUNTY GOVERNMENT:
       Section 1 - That Section 3.104(1) of Appendix A - Rules and Procedures of the Lexington-Fayette Urban County Council, be and hereby is amended to read as follows:
1)  The urban county council shall meet at the dates and times specified in a schedule of meetings adopted annually by the council by ordinance, in the council chamber on the second floor of the Lexington-Fayette Government Center, for purposes of conducting a "work session." Action taken by the urban county council at a work session is procedural in nature (See 2.201). A quorum for work sessions shall consist of not fewer than eight (8) of the fifteen (15) members of the council. The following order of business shall apply for work sessions of the urban county council;

I.  Public comment-agenda items only.

II. *Requested rezonings/docket approval. (No item shall be placed on the docket which has not been approved at work session, either as part of the work docket or as a separate item at work session, except in case of emergency and except as limited by section 4.07 of the Charter).

III. Approval of summary.

IV. *Budget amendments.

V. Budget adjustments (for information only).

VI. New business.

VII. Communications from the Mayor.

a. Appointments.

b. Donations.

c. Procurement Reports.
1. Price Contracts.
2. Fixed price bid recommendations (unilateral contract or purchase order).
3. Sole source procurement recommendations (unilateral contract or purchase order). 
VIII. Continuing business/presentations/employee recognition. Up to two presentations are permitted per work session and each presentation shall not exceed 15 minutes; up to one presentation can be LFUCG employee recognition.

IX. Council reports.

X. Public comment-issues not on agenda.
XI. Adjournment.
      
       Section 2 - That this Resolution shall become effective on the date of its passage. 
	PASSED URBAN COUNTY COUNCIL:

..title
An Ordinance amending Section 7-6 of the Code of Ordinances, pertaining to providing for an alternative process for the acceptance, approval, and establishment of price contracts for purchases for which funds have been Budgeted, to allow the same process to be used for fixed-price bids and sole source procurements that only require the Urban County Government to enter into a unilateral Contract or issue a Purchase Order, effective upon passage of Council. [Council Office, Hall] 
..body
      WHEREAS, the Urban County Government previously created and codified a more efficient and timely alternative process for the acceptance, approval, and establishment of price contracts for which funds have been Budgeted in Section 7-6 of the Code of Ordinances; and
      WHEREAS,  it is also more efficient and timely to have the option of using a similar process for procurements that only require the Urban County Government to enter into a unilateral Contract or a purchase order; and
      WHEREAS, including sufficient information on the Mayor's report for approval by Council ensures transparency with such procurement.
      NOW, THEREFORE, BE IT ORDAINED BY THE COUNCIL OF THE LEXINGTON-FAYETTE URBAN COUNTY GOVERNMENT:
      Section 1 - That Section 7-6 of the Lexington-Fayette Urban County Government Code of Ordinances be and hereby is amended to read as follows: 
Sec. 7-6. Alternative Approval Process for Price Contracts.  

(a) For purchases utilizing either: price contracts, or (II) fixed price bids or sole source procurements that only require the Urban County Government to enter into a unilateral Contract or issue a purchase order, and for which the funds have been Budgeted, the administration May place a summary of the acceptance, approval, and establishment of each such procurement on the Mayor's Report for Council approval in lieu of a Resolution for each procurement.

(b) At a minimum, the following information must be provided for each procurement: the name of the dept. or div. for which the procurement is being made, a description of the goods or services being procured, and the name(s) of the successful bidder(s).

(c) The Urban County Council May take any appropriate action with respect to any procurement item that is included in the Mayor's Report.

      Section 2 - To the extent any Ordinance or Resolution is in conflict with the provision of this Ordinance, the provisions of this Ordinance shall take precedence. 
      Section 3 - If any Section, subSection, sentence, clause, phrase, or portion of this Ordinance is for any reason held invalid or unlawful by a court of competent jurisdiction, such portion shall be deemed a separate, distinct, and independent provision and such holding shall not affect the validity of the remaining portions hereof.
      Section 4 - That this Ordinance shall become effective on the date of its passage. 
      PASSED URBAN COUNTY COUNCIL:

..Body
      WHEREAS, the Kentucky General Assembly has appropriated funds for infrastructure projects in House Bill 1 of the 2022 Regular Session of the Kentucky General Assembly for the Cleaner Water Program; and
      WHEREAS, the Lexington-Fayette Urban County Government (the "Grantee") has previously determined that it is in the public interest to design and construct certain facilities and improvements to the Grantee's utility system (the "Project"); and
      WHEREAS, the Grantee desires funding from the Kentucky Infrastructure Authority (the "Authority") for the purpose of acquisition and construction of the Project; and
      WHEREAS, in order to obtain a grant from the Cleaner Water Program for the Project, and administered by the Authority, the Grantee is required to enter into an assistance agreement (the "Agreement") with the Authority.
      NOW, THEREFORE, BE IT RESOLVED by the governing body of the Lexington-Fayette Urban County Government as follows:
      SECTION 1 - The Grantee hereby accepts the grant award and approves the Assistance Agreement between the Grantee and the Authority to provide the necessary funds to the Grantee for the Project.
      SECTION 2 - That the Mayor, on behalf of the Urban County Government, is hereby designated to be the Grantee's "Authorized Official" for this Project and is hereby directed and empowered by the Grantee to execute the Agreement, related documents and agreements, and to otherwise act on behalf of the Grantee to effect such grant award, and to engage a qualified Project Administrator.
      SECTION 3- That the Grantee hereby agrees and commits to include, by amendment to its annual budget and audit process, the receipts and expenditures of funds subject to the Agreement up to and including the date of Project closeout, and that subject to the provisions of Section 7-48 of the Lexington-Fayette Urban County Government Code of Ordinances, the Mayor is hereby authorized, in her discretion as the Chief Executive Officer of the Urban County Government, to transfer the unencumbered balance of any operating or capital account appropriation to another operating or account appropriation within the grant budget previously established for this grant.
      SECTION 4 - That this resolution shall take effect at the earliest time provided by law.
	ADOPTED on ___________202___.

Drafting Legislative Files
The drafting process is the same for any type of Legislative File you are creating in Legistar; the steps do not change only the information that is entered is different.  This draft guide illustrates creating a new file in a logical process, however it is not required that the information be entered in the manner described below.  

To begin from the main menu select Legislative Files from the left horizontal listing of main program headings.
How to open the Legislative Files Screen

1. Start at Legistar's Main Menu  
2. CLICK on the Legislative Files section in the left margin.  (Indicated by the arrow)  
3. The Legislative Files screen will open      


Legislative Files (Search Mode)
When you open the Legislative File screen it always opens in Search Mode which is displayed on the header bar shown below. Legistar is waiting for you to enter search criteria!   










How to place the screen in NEW Record Mode

1. Click on the NEW button.
2. The screen is now in New Record Mode as displayed on the top bar header bar.  Now you are ready to start entering the details of your new Legislative File.



Tips:
The screen shots in this guide illustrate the generic field labels and may vary from what you see on your screen.  When creating a new file in Legistar it is typical to go through the fields left to right in the order that they are seen on the screen.  

Working with your New File Defaults - Local Settings

When you click on New certain fields will automatically pre-fill with data.  This data comes from your local settings and are typical referred to as default entries.  These fields are:  File Type, File Status, Controlling Body and Created.  Typically, the Default File Status is "Draft."   The defaults should be set up to you most common scenario when creating a new file.  









Legislative File Fields Definitions

o FILE ID - The File ID is a unique number which is assigned to each file.   Typically, clients start with a permanent number in the format of the year YY -  NNNN or like this: 08 - 0000; temporary is just another numbering sequence that is set up and used by your organization until a permanent file id is assigned; leave as is allows you to select and leave the number as it was.  During the Legistar training you will be given the numbering sequence you are to use when drafting a new legislative file. 

o TYPE - The File Type is used to help group the file in the appropriate location on the agenda.  In addition, the file type is used in agenda grouping, searching and reporting.

o STATUS - The Status field is used to identify where the File is in the Legislative Process.  When clicking on NEW the default status is draft.  The Status is also used to group items on the agenda, searching and reporting.

o CONTROLLING BODY - The Controlling Body field will highlight which legislative body is currently is "in control" of the file.  This field is also used to determine agenda order and works with security restrictions.

o FILE CREATED DATE - The File Created Date, is the date in which the file was created or the NEW button was pressed in Legistar.  This date can be manually changed.

o AGENDA DATE - The Agenda Date is used to direct a legislative file to appear on a specific agenda.  The agenda date can be left blank and the legislative file will go to the next generated agenda for the controlling body it is assigned.

o FINAL ACTION DATE - The Final Action field will display the date of final action by your Council or Commission.  During file drafting data is not entered in this field.  If the final action date is present the file will not go to an agenda because Legistar assumes the file is completed when there is a final action date present. 

o TITLE - The Title field on the "Legislative Files" screen will be automatically populated with text you will input later in the ..Title section of the Text File field.  


Notes:
File Text

FILE TEXT TAB - The File Text Tab is the displays the verbiage of the Legislative file.  The text editor allows users to do their drafting and formatting directly within Legistar.   Legistar allows you two options when drafting:  1.) Legistar Drafting Editor or 2.) Microsoft Word.  The following steps outline how to draft in the Legistar Drafting Editor. 
How to Enter File Text into the Legistar Text Editor

1. To enter file text, click on the EDIT CURRENT button.  This opens the Legistar Drafting Editor. 

2. When the Text Editor opens you have several choices:  A) Click on New or click on the down arrow and select File Sections B) Insert a Template  C) Import your file from MS Word (rtf or txt).  

3. Click on NEW. When you click on the new button the Legistar Editor opens and pre-fills with the ..title and the ..body.  Just start typing the information directly into the Legistar Editor.  


Text Tips:
-The ..title is referred to as the agenda entry, the whereas portion is referred to as the body.  The ..title is used on 99% of the reports in Legistar and Daystar recommends that it not more than a paragraph long.  

-The title should be strictly subject related.  For example, if you place the words 'first reading' in the title it needs to be edited for the next time the file is on the agenda to 'second reading'.  This requires a user to manually change the text which is time consuming and allows for errors.  The workflow process is most efficient when the title is subject matter related allowing the headings and status to dictate the disposition of a file.  Therefore, the headings 'First Reading Ordinances' and 'Second Reading Ordinances' will reflect the position of the file and are not necessary in the title. 

-Formatting such as bullets, tabbing and other placement features are not recommended in Legistar.  This is because the text is placed on various reports and the formatting for one report may not work for another report.  If any formatting is desired Daystar recommends using the Microsoft Word editor as the performance has the results.  



Working with File Sections
File sections are sections of text which are used to show text on certain reports.  The key identifier for the text sections is the . . (dot, dot).  The ..title and the ..body are the generic file sections which are used throughout the Legistar system on various reports.   If a client has special report requirement a new file section could be added and a custom report can be developed to show the special section.

  












Tips:
-The dot dots should never be deleted.  This will cause the text not to show on the report.

-You cannot have duplicate alpha characters each file section has to be unique.   For example, you cannot have two sections that begin with "t" (..title and ..tax).
      Notes:
Working with Templates
If you have standard text that is used for certain file types templates can be added to the Legistar database.






















How to use a Template

1. Click the down arrow next to the "New" button.
2. Select the template that you would like to use.  Then template will be added in the Legistar editor screen and you can type the additional text where it belongs.

3. Click on "Go Back" and you will return to the main legislative files screen and can continue entering file detail.  

Without tabbing (Tab Key) or indenting, simply type the file detail directly below the appropriate ..section.  The .. are used to define different text sections, and to determine output on the Legistar Reports.  




Importing
Another option to get the text into the Legistar database is to use the import option.   When you import a document the text sections should be in the document (..title, ..body) 


How to Import the document
    
1. Click the down arrow next to the "New" button
2. Select Import from the menu 
3. Find the document and click on Open and the file will be brought into the Legistar editor.  You can now make any edits within the Legistar editor.

4. Click on "Go Back" and you will return to the main legislative files screen and can continue entering file detail.  

Tips:
Be sure that the document you are importing has been saved as .rtf or .txt and has the ..title and ..body identified.

After clicking "Go Back," the application will save information to the file and return you to the main "Legislative Files" screen.

You will also notice that whatever information was typed directly below ..Title in the "File Text" box automatically populated the  "Title" field.



Working with Microsoft Word 
When Microsoft Word opens the Legistar Tool bar will be shown as part of an option from the toolbar.  From the drop down arrow on the Legistar toolbar decide whether to use a template or select a section.

 


How to Draft in Microsoft Word

    
1. Click on the Edit Current Button and Microsoft Word will open.  
2. From the Microsoft Word menu you will see a Legistar button (see below) which is referred to as the Legistar toolbar. 

3. The Legistar toolbar will offer the same options as the Legistar editor.  You can add a template, add a specific section or insert a file from the Microsoft Word header button "Insert" then select file and find the appropriate file to insert.  You can now make any edits within the Legistar editor.




4. From the Legistar toolbar select save, then you will receive a confirmation message stating that the "File Text is saved."  Microsoft Word will close and the text is brought back to the main Legislative Files screen and can continue entering file detail.  


After you have saved the Microsoft Word document it will take you back to the main Legislative Files screen.  





History Tab 

The history tabs records all of the actions that have been taking on the file along with the votes and any discussion recorded during your Meeting Minutes.   In addition, the history criteria will display any meetings that the item has scheduled.   During the drafting process, there will not be any history lines.










History Criteria

Past Action - Shows action which has taken place on meeting that are completed.
Scheduled Meetings - Shows a line letting the user know that this item is scheduled for a meeting.
Show All - show both past action and scheduled meeting lines.











Attachments Tab 
On the Attachments tab you will find what most client's call Supporting Documentation.  These would include any backup documents that would be submitted for the agenda.  You can have unlimited attachments of any file type.  However, it is recommended that most attachments be in PDF so all users can open them without the need for special software. 




















ATTACHMENT NAME - This is the name of the attachment. You will see the attachment name in the Attachments box on the left and the Attachment Name field on the right. 

DESCRIPTION - This field allows for free text typing describing each individual attachment.

EXPIRATION DATE - If an attachment is no longer valid after a certain date, users can place that information here.  Note:  Attachments WILL NOT be automatically removed, this is just a descriptive field.

PRINT THIS ATTACHMENT WITH REPORTS - Checking this field will allow the attachment to print with certain Legistar Reports.

SHOW THIS ATTACHMENT ON INTERNET REPORTS - Checking this field will create a link to this attachment on Internet reports.

Note:  Both the "Print This Attachment with Reports" and "Show This Attachment On Internet Reports" are checked by default.  If you do not want a particular attachment to print or show up on the internet, these boxes should be unchecked.


How to Add an Attachment
1.  Click the Import button located at the bottom left side of the screen.

2. Double click on file located

3. The document is now attached.


Re-Naming an Attachments 
An attachment CAN be removed once it has been brought into Legistar by typing a new name in the Attachment Name field and clicking on the Update Attachment Details button.

Details Tab 
These fields can help provide more specific information about the file.  


















FILE NAME - The File Name field is the short title.  This field can be used on the form of the agenda, display a few key words to the processor so they can easily recognize the file.

REQUESTER - Use of the Requester field represents the Service Area/Unit that requested that this file.

CONTACT - Enter your Service Area Administrator or other contact name as directed by your Area. This is a free text field so you type this information directly into the field.

NOTES - The Notes field is provided as a communication tool. Input notes you may want the approver or others to know about the item here.

COST - If a cost is associated with file enter the total amount into the Cost field.

DRAFTER - Enter the preparer's name or other contact as directed by your Area. This is a free text field so you type this information directly into the field.

HEARING DATE - If a public hearing date is associated with this item, you may enter the date in this field. It is for reference only.


Associations Tab 

This tab provides users with an easy way to index and reference their legislation.  These fields perform an EITHER search, meaning that the more information placed in these fields, the more results you will likely receive.  These are the only fields on the Legislative Files Screen to work in this manner.




















CODE SECTIONS - This section allows the users to attach related code sections to a File.  The Code Sections are used to reference our City Code.

INDEXES - An Index is used to reference a Legislative File to a certain topic.

SPONSORS - The Sponsor is the individual Councilmember or a number of Councilmembers that represents an active stand regarding the legislative File.  A Legislative File can have several sponsors.

RELATED FILES - This field is used to highlight a relationship between Legislative Files.

Authorization to execute a Conditional Commitment Letter and accept additional federal funding from the Kentucky Cleaner Water Round 2 Grant (American Rescue Plan Act funds) in the amount of $990,202 for the East Hickman Pump Station Expansion and Rehabilitation Consent Decree project, bringing the total project cost to $3,770,202. ..Body
WHEREAS, the Kentucky General Assembly has appropriated funds for infrastructure projects in Senate Bill 36 of the 2021 Regular Session of the Kentucky General Assembly and in House Bill 1 of the 2022 Regular Session of the Kentucky General Assembly for the Cleaner Water Program; and
WHEREAS, the Lexington-Fayette Urban County Government (the "Grantee") has previously determined that it is in the public interest to design and construct certain facilities and improvements to the Grantee's utility system (the "Project"); and
WHEREAS, the Grantee desires funding from the Kentucky Infrastructure Authority (the "Authority") for the purpose of acquisition and construction of the Project; and
WHEREAS, in order to obtain a supplemental grant from the Cleaner Water Program for the Project, and administered by the Authority, the Grantee is required to enter into a supplemental assistance agreement (the "Agreement") with the Authority.
NOW, THEREFORE, BE IT RESOLVED by the governing body of the Lexington-Fayette Urban County Government as follows:
SECTION 1 - The Grantee hereby accepts the grant award and approves the Agreement between the Grantee and the Authority to provide the additional funds to the Grantee for the Project.
SECTION 2 - That the Mayor, on behalf of the Urban County Government, is hereby designated to be the Grantee's "Authorized Official" for this Project and is hereby directed and empowered by the Grantee to execute the Agreement, related documents and agreements, and to otherwise act on behalf of the Grantee to effect such grant award, and to engage a qualified Project Administrator.
SECTION 3 - That the Grantee hereby agrees and commits to include, by amendment to its annual budget and audit process, the receipts and expenditures of funds subject to the Agreement up to and including the date of Project closeout, and that subject to the provisions of Section 7-48 of the Lexington-Fayette Urban County Government Code of Ordinances, the Mayor is hereby authorized, in her discretion as the Chief Executive Officer of the Urban County Government, to transfer the unencumbered balance of any operating or capital account appropriation to another operating or account appropriation within the grant budget previously established for this grant.
SECTION 4 - That this resolution shall take effect at the earliest time provided by law.

matters.title: A Resolution authorizing the Div. of Police to purchase eSOPH Background Checks System from NEOGOV, a sole source provider, and authorizing the Mayor, on behalf of the Urban County Government, to execute any necessary Agreement with NEOGOV, related to the procurement at a cost not to exceed $16,951. [Div. of Police, Weathers]
matters.text:
..Title
Request Council Authorization to accept the attached Quote and Sole Source Certification with PowerDMS by NEOGOV for the eSOPH Background Checks System.  eSOPH will be used by the Background and Polygraph Units as a cloud-based system which will streamline much of the background hiring process.  This platform will allow investigators to have sole source to access their candidate’s information, and forms, while allowing candidates to upload and complete necessary forms for investigator access.  eSOPH will also make tracking candidates much easier than manually entering information into Excel.  In doing so, the time it takes to conduct a thorough background investigations should be shortened significantly with the use of live forms and a platform that can be accessed via tablet, smart phone, laptop, or desktop.  The Lexington Police Department is requesting approval from the Urban County Council to authorize Mayor Gorton to sign the attached documents.  Upon signing, please return to the Chief’s Office to acquire additional signatures.  Funds are budgeted.

If you have any questions or require additional information, please contact my office.

Authorization to execute an Amended and Restated Supplemental Grant Assistance Agreement for the federal award from the Kentucky Cleaner Water Round 2 Grant (American Rescue Plan Act funds) awarded in the amount of $3,770,202 for the East Hickman Pump Station Expansion and Rehabilitation project. ..Body
WHEREAS, the Kentucky General Assembly has appropriated funds for infrastructure projects in House Bill 1 of the 2022 Regular Session of the Kentucky General Assembly for the Cleaner Water Program; and
WHEREAS, the Lexington-Fayette Urban County Government (the "Grantee") has previously determined that it is in the public interest to design and construct certain facilities and improvements to the Grantee's utility system (the "Project"); and
WHEREAS, the Grantee desires funding from the Kentucky Infrastructure Authority (the "Authority") for the purpose of acquisition and construction of the Project; and
WHEREAS, in order to obtain a Grant from the Cleaner Water Program for the Project, and administered by the Authority, the Grantee is required to enter into an assistance Agreement (the "Agreement") with the Authority.
NOW, THEREFORE, BE IT RESOLVED by the governing body of the Lexington-Fayette Urban County Government as follows:
SECTION 1 - The Grantee hereby accepts the Grant award and approves the Assistance Agreement between the Grantee and the Authority to provide the necessary funds to the Grantee for the Project.
SECTION 2 - That the Mayor, on behalf of the Urban County Government, is hereby designated to be the Grantee's "Authorized Official" for this Project and is hereby directed and empowered by the Grantee to execute the Agreement, related documents and Agreements, and to otherwise act on behalf of the Grantee to effect such Grant award, and to engage a qualified Project Administrator.
SECTION 3 - That the Grantee hereby agrees and commits to include, by Amendment to its annual Budget and audit process, the receipts and expenditures of funds subject to the Agreement up to and including the date of Project closeout, and that subject to the provisions of Section 7-48 of the Lexington-Fayette Urban County Government Code of Ordinances, after providing a revised Budget to KIA, the Mayor is hereby authorized, in her discretion as the Chief Executive Officer of the Urban County Government, to transfer the unencumbered balance of any operating or capital account appropriation to another operating or account appropriation within the Grant Budget previously established for this Grant.
SECTION 4 - That this Resolution shall take effect at the earliest time provided by law.
	ADOPTED on ___________2026.
